facts.text: The goals expressed in the Preamble are the characteristic features of the Constitution as well.
facts.quote: The goals expressed in the Preamble are the characteristic features of our Constitution as well.

facts.text: The federal system is one of the important features of the Constitution; countries with large territories and huge populations are run by a federal system.
facts.quote: One of the important features of our Constitution is the federal system. In countries with large territories and huge populations, government is run by a federal system.

facts.text: Ruling a large territory from a single capital city is difficult and may lead to neglect of far-flung areas.
facts.quote: Ruling a large territory from a single capital city is not only difficult, but may also lead to the neglect of some far-flung areas.

facts.text: Governments function at two levels in a federation.
facts.quote: Therefore, Governments function at two levels in a federation.

facts.text: The Government at the Centre handles defence, foreign policy and establishing peace; it is also called the Union Government or Federal Government.
facts.quote: The Government at the Centre carries out tasks like defence of the entire country, foreign policy, establishing peace, etc. It is also called 'Union Government' or 'Federal Government'.

facts.text: The State Government looks after the administration of a particular State, e.g. the Government of Maharashtra.
facts.quote: It looks after the administration of a particular State. For example, Government of Maharashtra looks after the administration of the State of Maharashtra.

facts.text: Federalism is running the administration of a country cooperatively by Governments at two levels, making laws about different subjects.
facts.quote: The system of running the administration of a country cooperatively by the Governments at two levels, making laws about different subjects is called federalism.

facts.text: Separation of Powers: the Constitution divides subjects for making laws and has given three lists of subjects.
facts.quote: The Constitution has divided the subjects for making laws between the Union Government and the State Governments. ... Our Constitution has given three lists of various subjects.

facts.text: The Union List contains 97 subjects on which the Union Government makes laws.
facts.quote: The first list is called Union List. It contains 97 subjects on which the Union Government makes laws.

facts.text: The State List, for the State Governments, contains 66 subjects.
facts.quote: The State List is for the State Governments to legislate upon. It contains 66 subjects.

facts.text: The Concurrent List contains 47 subjects; both Governments can make laws on them.
facts.quote: there is a Concurrent List, which contains 47 subjects. Both Governments can make laws on subjects included in this list.

facts.text: If a subject is not in any list, the Union Government makes laws on it; these are Residuary Powers.
facts.quote: If a subject comes up that is not included in any of the lists, the Union Government is entitled to make laws on it. These powers are termed as Residuary Powers.

facts.text: Union Government subjects: defence, foreign relations, war and peace, currency, international trade.
facts.quote: Subjects with the Union Government : Defence, foreign relations, war and peace, currency, international trade, etc.

facts.text: State Government subjects: agriculture, law and order, local government, health, prison administration.
facts.quote: Subjects with the State Government : Agriculture, law and order, local government, health, prison administration, etc.

facts.text: Subjects with both Governments: employment, environment, economic and social planning, personal law, education.
facts.quote: Subjects with both the Governments : Employment, environment, economic and social planning, personal law, education, etc.

facts.text: The division of powers is unique; it lets the Union and State Governments cooperate and encourages citizens' participation.
facts.quote: The division of powers in the Indian Constitution is unique. ... This also encourages participation of citizens in the administration of the country.

facts.text: India has a Union Government, 28 State Governments and 9 Union Territories; the Union Government controls the Union Territories.
facts.quote: In India, there is a Union Government, 28 State Governments and 9 Union Territories. The Union Government controls the Union Territories.

facts.text: The nine Union Territories: New Delhi, Daman and Diu, Puducherry, Chandigarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh and Lakshadweep.
facts.quote: Following are the nine Union Territories : New Delhi, Daman and Diu, Puducherry, Chandigarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh and Lakshadweep.

facts.text: Currency notes carry the words 'Guaranteed by the Central Government'.
facts.quote: The words 'Guaranteed by the Central Government' are printed on currency notes.

facts.text: A policeman's badge reads 'Maharashtra Police'.
facts.quote: If you have seen the badge on the uniform of a policeman, it reads 'Maharashtra Police.'

facts.text: Examples like Indian Railways and Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation show that Government functions at two levels.
facts.quote: 'Indian Railways' and 'Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation'. This means that in our country, Government functions at two levels.

facts.text: In the parliamentary system the Parliament, i.e. the Legislature, has the highest decision-making power.
facts.quote: In such a system, the Parliament, i.e. the Legislature has the highest decision-making power.

facts.text: Indian Parliament includes the President, Lok Sabha (House of the People) and Rajya Sabha (Council of States).
facts.quote: Indian Parliament includes the President, Lok Sabha or the House of the People and Rajya Sabha or the Council of States.

facts.text: The Council of Ministers emerges from the Lok Sabha and is answerable to it for all its decisions.
facts.quote: The Council of Ministers that runs the administration emerges from the Lok Sabha and is answerable to the Lok Sabha for all its decisions.

facts.text: In Parliamentary Democracy, discussion and debates in the Parliament have great significance.
facts.quote: In Parliamentary Democracy, the discussion and debates that take place in the Parliament have great significance.

facts.text: The Constitution created an independent Judiciary; disputes not resolved mutually go to it, and the Court hears both parties impartially.
facts.quote: The Indian Constitution has created an independent Judiciary. The disputes that cannot be resolved mutually are referred to the Judiciary. The Court hears both the contesting parties ... This has to be done impartially.

facts.text: Judges are appointed by the President, not by the Government, and it is not easy to remove them.
facts.quote: Judges are appointed by the President and not by the Government. It is not easy to remove the Judges from their office.

facts.text: The Constitution has granted a single citizenship to all Indians: 'Indian Citizenship'.
facts.quote: The Indian Constitution has granted a single citizenship to all Indians. That is 'Indian Citizenship.'

facts.text: Frequent amendments may lead to instability, so the amendment procedure is specified in the Constitution itself.
facts.quote: frequent amendments to the Constitution may lead to a situation of instability. The procedure for amendment is specified in the Constitution itself

facts.text: The amendment procedure is unique: neither too difficult nor too easy, and flexible for general amendments.
facts.quote: The procedure for amendment in the Constitution is unique. It is neither too difficult, nor too easy. ... The procedure is also flexible to ensure that general amendments can be brought about easily.

facts.text: The Election Commission is the independent machinery responsible for conducting all elections in India.
facts.quote: This machinery is known as the Election Commission. The responsibility of conducting all elections in India rests with the Election Commission.

facts.text: If the government conducted elections, there might be no guarantee of a free, fair and just atmosphere.
facts.quote: If the government were to conduct elections, there might be no guarantee of such free, fair and just atmosphere for the elections.

facts.text: Another important feature of the Constitution is the exhaustive provision of fundamental rights.
facts.quote: Another important feature of our Constitution is the exhaustive provision of fundamental rights.

facts.text: Chandigarh is the capital of Chandigarh Union Territory and the States of Punjab and Haryana.
facts.quote: Chandigarh is the capital of Chandigarh Union Territory and the States of Punjab and Haryana.
